title: Field engine refuses a wide tool's short move on the per-move cell ceiling; the column engine cuts it

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`SdfField::subtract_batch` (`field_cut.rs`) refuses a chord when its swept window, clipped to the cut region, spans more than `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` (1 << 22) cells. The message asks the caller to segment the move. For a wide tool, the tool's own footprint already passes the ceiling. Then a 1 mm move is refused, and segmenting cannot help.

The column engine cuts the same move. `backend.rs` says that refusals are backend-independent. This refusal is reached by a valid short move that the column arm accepts.

Measured on 6c9e5f1e7 (v0.26.0; `field_cut.rs`, `field_batch.rs` and `field_sweep.rs` are the same on main 034e91b8b), a synthetic block, cell 0.254 mm, one 1 mm feed move of a flat tool 50.8 mm across:

| Engine | Result |
|---|---|
| Column | cuts |
| Field | refused on op 0: "a chord's swept window spans more than" 1 << 22 "cells at cell size 0.254 - the move is too long for one field update; segment it" |

The tool's footprint alone is about 201 x 201 cells. With the block's height in the window, a zero-length move would pass the ceiling too.

We found it in our own lane at the same cell size: a disc head 127.4 mm across on a 44.45 mm neck (through `simulate_undercut`) and a flat tool 50.8 mm across over 33.7 mm of stock. Both were refused on their first move.

### Why it looks like a policy limit, not a memory limit

`cut_batch` keeps only a brick-to-sweep list. `cut_brick` dismisses a brick that the sweep cannot reach by one test at the brick centre. The work of a wide tool's short move is the bricks that it meets. Memory does not grow with the window.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `Stock::block(Backend::Field { band: FIELD_BAND }, 0.0, 0.0, 120.0, 120.0, 30.0, 0.254)`.
2. `simulate` one feed move from (60, 60, 25) to (61, 60, 25) with a flat tool of radius 25.4.
3. The field engine returns `Err` (the ceiling). The same steps on `Backend::Column` return `Ok`.

Expected: both cut.

### Proposed fix

Let the ceiling bound what segmenting can bound: the cells of the chord's clipped window beyond the cells of the tool at rest at the chord's start (the same clipping). A short move of any tool then passes. A long chord still refuses with the same message, and segmenting always brings it under the ceiling. Pin: the steps above cut on both engines. Keep a pin that a long chord of a normal tool still refuses.

The f32 cut twin (`cut_twin_work.rs`, `TWIN_MAX_CELLS_PER_CHORD`) states the same value. We would keep it as it is in this fix and list it as a follow-up, unless you prefer both in one change.

### Version and OS

6c9e5f1e7 (v0.26.0, source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `P3`.
